claims.text: Conventional EAM reference models inadequately represent the configurational diversity of ab initio liquids in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references exhibit significant reference–target phase-space mismatch in the liquid state.
MLIPs should replace conventional EAM references in free-energy calculations for high-entropy alloys near melting.
The MLIPs should be trained on ab initio data covering a wide range of local atomic configurations.
The MLIP training set should include both solid and ab initio liquid configurations.
Training on solid and liquid ab initio configurations will allow the MLIP to capture more complex local bonding and a richer spectrum of configurations than EAM.
Capturing this broader configurational spectrum will make the MLIP energy landscape more representative of the ab initio target landscape.
A more representative MLIP energy landscape will improve phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Improved phase-space overlap will produce a shorter and smoother thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLIP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
An MLIP that properly reproduces liquid configurational complexity will improve free-energy calculation accuracy.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys, described as typically having five or more principal components.
The proposed method applies to compositions spanning solid-to-liquid phase stability near the melting temperature, with modest compositional fluctuations.
The benefit of an MLIP reference will be greatest near high melting temperatures and in systems with substantial configurational diversity.
The benefit may diminish far from melting or in simpler, less multicomponent systems.
Failure to reduce path mismatch by at least approximately 20% relative to the EAM control would falsify the hypothesis.
